raw_case_text: A 58-year-old male had a history of end-stage renal failure with 3 kidney transplantations (1979, 1981 and 2008). He had previous chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever and cytomegalovirus infection. The last renal transplantation was associated with acute rejection requiring a combination of anti-thymoglobulin, plasma exchanges, rituximab, mycophenolate mofetil 1g/d, tacrolimus 4.5mg/d and prednisone 10 mg/d. In 2004 Leishmania PCR in blood was positive (Fig 1B). L-AmB treatment initially induced clinical cure. Relapse occurred in August 2009 when plasma exchanges and corticosteroids boluses were administered for the graft rejection. Fever, anemia (Hb = 9.1g/dL) and leukopenia (leukocytes = 1600/mm3) were observed, along with 431 Leishmania per ml of blood (assessed by quantitative PCR). L-AmB (induction total dose, 40 mg/Kg) provided improvement and reduced parasitemia to 6.9 Leishmania/ml. A second recurrence with fever and a rise in parasitemia to 29.6 Leishmania/ml occurred in January 2010 during monthly maintenance administration of 3 mg/kg of L-AmB. High-dose L-AmB was reintroduced followed by miltefosine for 4 months. Parasitemia decreased but remained positive (0.4 Leishmania/ml) and number of CD4 lymphocytes increased from 87 to 147/mm3. A third recurrence was reported in July 2010 with fever, 29.8 Leishmania/ml and positive Leishmania culture from venous blood. L-AmB was reintroduced, followed by maintenance infusions for 4 months, 3 mg/Kg every 3 weeks plus downgrading of immunosuppressive therapies. As symptoms persisted, infusions were performed once-weekly and then twice-weekly. Parasitemia decreased from 88 to 0.6 Leishmania/ml but a fourth recurrence occurred in April-June 2011 with fever, leukopenia (leukocytes = 1200/mm3, CD4 lymphocytes = 186/mm3), anemia (Hb = 9.1g/dL) and parasitemia at 40 Leishmania/ml. Patient refused to increase the L-AmB dose, it continued at 3 mg/Kg twice-weekly. Transplant nephrectomy was performed in November 2011 and chronic dialysis reinstituted. In February 2012, fever, splenomegaly, anemia (Hb = 8.6g/dL) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count = 50,000/mm3) were observed with 12,870 Leishmania/ml and 60,440 Leishmania/ml of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Thereafter, meglumine antimoniate adapted to renal clearance was administered daily for 28 days, then 1-3 times/week for maintenance. Liver function remained normal. ECG showed a T-wave inversion but troponin remained normal. Fever and sweats resolved, spleen size decreased from 21 to 17 cm, and blood counts normalized in 4 weeks, number of CD4 lymphocytes = 833/mm3 in June 2012,. Leishmania blood PCR and cultures became negative within a month and remained negative over eight monthly evaluations until death in January 2013 due to hypovolemic shock following a dental extraction.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old male renal transplant recipient presented with recurrent fever, anemia, and leukopenia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 58-year-old male with end-stage renal disease and three kidney transplantations presented with recurrent fevers. He had an initial parasitic infection in 2004 that responded to liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB). Relapse occurred in August 2009 during treatment for graft rejection with fever, anemia, and leukopenia, which improved following high-dose L-AmB. A second recurrence occurred in January 2010 on monthly L-AmB maintenance, managed with L-AmB and 4 months of miltefosine. A third recurrence occurred in July 2010, requiring biweekly then twice-weekly L-AmB infusions. A fourth relapse occurred in April-June 2011 with persistent fever and cytopenias. Following transplant nephrectomy and resumption of dialysis in November 2011, he experienced another severe relapse in February 2012 with pulmonary involvement, splenomegaly, and severe thrombocytopenia.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal failure with three renal transplantations (1979, 1981, 2008); acute graft rejection treated with anti-thymocyte globulin, plasma exchange, rituximab, mycophenolate mofetil (1 g/day), tacrolimus (4.5 mg/day), and prednisone (10 mg/day). History of chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever, and CMV infection. Transplant nephrectomy performed November 2011; maintained on chronic hemodialysis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Recurrent high-grade fevers, drenching diaphoresis, fatigue, malaise. Denied hemoptysis, chest pain, or gastrointestinal bleeding.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile and diaphoretic. Palpable splenomegaly measuring 21 cm in longitudinal diameter (regressed to 17 cm, then non-palpable post-treatment). Hemodialysis vascular access functional. No peripheral edema.
objective.routine_investigations: August 2009: hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, leukocytes 1,600/mm^3. January 2010: CD4+ count increased from 87 to 147/mm^3. April 2011: hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, leukocytes 1,200/mm^3, CD4+ count 186/mm^3. February 2012: hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL, platelets 50,000/mm^3. June 2012: CD4+ count 833/mm^3 with normalized blood counts. Liver function tests remained normal throughout. Troponin levels normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) performed during pulmonary manifestation. Electrocardiogram (ECG) demonstrated T-wave inversion with normal cardiac enzymes.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Recurrent visceral leishmaniasis with pulmonary involvement in an immunosuppressed renal allograft recipient on hemodialysis.
Diagnostic Confirmation: Quantitative PCR of peripheral blood demonstrated parasitemia across episodes: 431 Leishmania/mL in August 2009; 29.6 Leishmania/mL in January 2010; 29.8 Leishmania/mL with positive blood culture in July 2010; 40 Leishmania/mL in 2011; and 12,870 Leishmania/mL in peripheral blood and 60,440 Leishmania/mL in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in February 2012.
Differentials Ruled Out: Acute allograft rejection versus bacterial/viral sepsis, Q fever reactivation, cytomegalovirus viremia, and tuberculosis.
Treatment & Clinical Course: Received sequential courses of liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB; induction 40 mg/kg, then maintenance 3 mg/kg biweekly to twice-weekly) and oral miltefosine for 4 months with down-titration of immunosuppression. In February 2012, meglumine antimoniate adjusted for renal clearance was administered daily for 28 days, followed by 1-3 times weekly maintenance. Spleen normalized, hematologic parameters recovered, CD4+ count reached 833/mm^3, and Leishmania PCR and blood cultures remained negative over 8 monthly evaluations until death in January 2013 from hypovolemic shock following dental extraction.
